prospect.name: Jorge Lourenço
prospect.location: Portugal (Algarve — 'Jaguar' in the transcript is an ASR artefact)
prospect.training_background: Long-term gym-goer, cancelled his gym subscription the day before the call; currently trains MMA twice a week and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu three times a week; has an outdoor training area and a pull-up bar at home
prospect.medical: Back and shoulder pain for several years, self-described as recurring rather than chronic, worse with training volume; manages it by visiting a chiropractor. Discloses heavy alcohol use and 'some drugs'; on the day of the call was doing a 24-hour fast because of it.

signals: Already trains five sessions a week in combat sport — 'It doesn't sound like you're in terrible shape. No.'
Explicitly good-to-great framing: 'Because I want to be in a better shape... more energy and be more agile'
Has savings and an active stock portfolio, but price was still a hard barrier — 'It's not worth for me $6,000' — which is the one place he departs from the pure optimizer profile

goals.text: Get rid of the recurring back and shoulder pain
Build muscle mass, particularly legs — 'develop some mass'
Train at home rather than at a gym
Perform better in BJJ/MMA sparring — stop losing to weaker opponents
Build better habits and cut down the drinking
Be a visible role model so his children learn the lifestyle by example

pains.text: Recurring back and shoulder pain for years despite training a lot — 'I'm always in some kind of pain'
Alcohol use costs him three to four days of recovery and he gets beaten in sparring by weaker opponents
Disclosed drug use alongside alcohol as the worst part of his habits
Has to push through pain to play with his 6- and 4-year-old
Decided 2-3 months ago to start kettlebells and has still done nothing
Gym became boring; cancelled the subscription
Legs will not grow despite training them

objections.raw_quote: It's super expensive. I wasn't thinking about that. I was thinking about it. I was like three hundred dollars. The euros per month or something like this.
objections.rep_response: Asked whether it was impossible or a matter of figuring it out, isolated intent, asked about monthly surplus, then moved off the $6,000 offer entirely to an unlisted $1,000/6mo self-serve programme

objections.raw_quote: I'll be honest. I searched online, and then after, and I thought there was something like $200.
objections.rep_response: 'I would say what you saw online, because I know what you're talking about, that that's something completely different' — then sold him that cheaper thing anyway a minute later

objections.raw_quote: let me think about it and talk with my wife, that's it
objections.rep_response: Asked whether she would be supportive and what she might say if she said no; did not run the responsibility/permission reframe or offer a refundable deposit

objections.raw_quote: Okay, but I think I wouldn't do it with the 6,000. With the 1,000, maybe, let me think about it and talk with my wife, that's it.
objections.rep_response: Agreed to send a written email describing what is included and to follow up after he speaks to his wife

offer.payment_plan_terms: On the unlisted self-serve tier only. Rep first said '$1,000 for six months. We can also do 200 a month, but that's sort of throwing away 200', then two turns later said 'it's 1,000 for six months. If you want to do it per month, it would be $600 a month.' The two monthly figures contradict each other and neither was corrected before the call ended. No instalment option was offered against the $6,000 coaching.

evidence: Prospect declined the main offer outright: 'No, it's too much for sure' and 'It's not worth for me $6,000'
On the downsell he said 'Yeah, I can do it' and 'No, I want to do it', but then conditioned it: 'let me think about it and talk with my wife'
Asked for written collateral first: 'Can you send me an email to see what is included on this site'
No payment link was sent on the call — the rep said 'I will send you the link for it' contingent on the wife conversation, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link-sent rule does not apply
Counter-evidence: intent on the cheaper tier was genuinely strong and the wife was described as supportive
outcome.next_step: Rep sends an email itemising what the self-serve programme includes; prospect speaks to his wife that evening and replies the next day

notable.note: Prospect disclosed 'the worst thing is alcohol, and some drugs' at 00:09:18. The rep replied 'I like the honesty' and never returned to the drug disclosure at any point, including while building a nutrition and accountability plan explicitly around alcohol reduction. Two contradictory monthly prices ($200/month and $600/month) were quoted for the same $1,000 six-month product within ninety seconds and neither was corrected.

quality.notes: Heavy and sustained swapping — most question/answer pairs in the 00:09-00:20 and 00:31-00:39 ranges are inverted relative to their labels, including the price-reveal block where the $6,000 figure appears under the prospect's label. Roles resolved from content throughout. Prospect's English is non-native and several turns are partially garbled; the 'Jaguar' location reference is an ASR artefact.
